title: 2003 HMMT February Geometry Problem 9
statement: In triangle \(A B C, \angle A B C=50^{\circ}\) and \(\angle A C B=70^{\circ}\). Let \(D\) be the midpoint of side \(B C\). A circle is tangent to \(B C\) at \(B\) and is also tangent to segment \(A D\); this circle instersects \(A B\) again at \(P\). Another circle is tangent to \(B C\) at \(C\) and is also tangent to segment \(A D\); this circle intersects \(A C\) again at \(Q\). Find \(\angle A P Q\) (in degrees).

solutions.text:
70
Suppose the circles are tangent to \(A D\) at \(E, F\), respectively; then, by equal tangents, \(D E=D B=D C=D F \Rightarrow E=F\) (as shown). So, by the Power of a Point Theorem, \(A P \cdot A B=A E^{2}=A F^{2}=A Q \cdot A C \Rightarrow A P / A Q=A C / A B \Rightarrow \triangle A P Q \sim \triangle A C B\), giving \(\angle A P Q=\angle A C B=70^{\circ}\).
